method: All residual OTHER titles (449 under v1, read in two hash-ordered passes of 170 and 110 plus counts over the remainder) were read manually; a label was added or extended only when it covered >=15 titles across >=3 channels and stayed mutually understandable. New labels sit last in priority, so they can only relabel former OTHER titles (primary) while Title_Archetypes_All records them everywhere they match.

decisions.POV: EXTENDED (not new): second-person scenario/role-play openers ("Your life as...", "You're the...", "Why it sucks to be...", "What it's like to be...") were missing from the POV rule; large, cross-channel pattern.
decisions.STORY_NARRATIVE: NEW: third-person true-story/profile titles ("The Spy Who...", "He Stole..."). Validated by size and 4+ channels but heavily concentrated in one history channel, so any finding about it is CHANNEL_CLUSTERED.
decisions.TRAP_OR_LIE: NEW: "the X trap / lie / scam / illusion", "keeping you poor". Validated across 6+ channels, mostly finance.
decisions.NAMED_FRAMEWORK: NEW: a named rule/formula/strategy/system/method. Validated across 7+ channels, finance-heavy.

rejected_candidates.BENCHMARK (milestones/averages/stats by: rejected: 23 residual titles, only 3 channels, all one finance template family; regex mixes concepts
rejected_candidates.PERSONAL_EXPERIMENT (\"I drank X for 7 d: rejected as new label: 6 titles, one channel; extended CASE_STUDY verbs instead
rejected_candidates.HASHTAG_ONLY: rejected: 8 titles; these carry no packaging information, left in OTHER
rejected_candidates.CHALLENGE / PREDICTION / VERSUS / RANKIN: no recurring pattern in the 280+ OTHER titles read (COMPARISON already exists)

residual_note: Residual OTHER is mostly finance declarative claim titles from three sister finance channels, hashtag/label-only titles and one-off topic titles; no further label met the threshold.
